title: Cryptolog Evidence Contract and Key Rotation Orchestration
content:
Purpose:
This document defines an evidence contract for key-management lifecycle events and a practical orchestration runbook for automated rotation and SIEM export. It connects RBAC v2 roles to required audit outputs, specifies a compact audit log schema for SIEM ingestion (ECS-friendly), and describes an automated evidence packaging pipeline for compliance audits. It is intended for platform security, SRE, and compliance engineers working on BYOK, HSM fallback, and envelope encryption patterns.

High-level goals:
- Produce deterministic, queryable evidence for every key lifecycle change (create, import, rotate, revoke, escrow, expire, backup, restore).
- Map RBAC v2 permissions to audit obligations and enforcement checkpoints.
- Provide a machine-readable audit log schema that can be exported to SIEM without transformation loss.
- Automate bundling and notarization of evidence for periodic audits and incident response.
- Define fallback behavior for HSM unavailability and BYOK import edge cases.

Principles and assumptions:
- All KMS operations must produce an immutable audit event within 1s of operation completion (best-effort).
- Evidence bundles SHALL be signed by a rotation coordinator service key and optionally wrapped with customer keys for BYOK customers.
- RBAC v2 is authoritative for who can initiate each operation; policy evaluation results must be included as part of the event.
- SIEM ingestion uses ECS-compatible fields; downstream parsers rely on stable field names in the contract.

RBAC v2 role-to-operation matrix (summary):
- role:kms-key-admin -> allow: create_key, import_key_material, rotate_key, schedule_rotation, set_rotation_policy, revoke_key, decrypt_metadata
- role:kms-operator -> allow: view_key_metadata, initiate_rotation, approve_manual_rotate, query_audit_logs
- role:platform-auditor -> allow: read_audit_stream, download_evidence_bundles (read-only)
- role:tenant-admin -> allow: request_byok-import, bind_customer_key, view_key_status (tenant-scoped)
- role:incident-runner -> allow: emergency-rotation (requires 2nd factor + approval token)

Each role must be accompanied in the audit event with: principal_id, principal_type, auth_method (oauth|mTLS|api-key), policy_evaluation_id.

Audit event schema (compact, flat, ECS-friendly):
- event_id: unique-uuid (string)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string
- event_type: one of [key.create,key.import,key.rotate,key.revoke,key.backup,key.restore,key.policy.update,key.escrow,key.fallback.hsm]
- key_id: opaque identifier (string)
- key_alias: optional human alias (string)
- tenant_id: optional tenant id or '-': multi-tenant scoping
- operation_result: SUCCESS | FAIL | PENDING
- initiator_principal: principal id string
- initiator_role: RBAC role name string
- auth_method: oauth|mTLS|api-key|ssh|console
- policy_evaluation_id: id (string)
- audit_proof_crc: short hex checksum of evidence artifacts (see packaging)
- hsm_slot: optional HSM slot id or 'n/a'
- kms_node: runtime node id handling operation
- rotation_policy_version: semantic version or 'none'
- kms_build_sha: runtime build sha for binary provenance
- extra: optional freeform short tags (CSV)

Example raw audit event (as emitted):
{
  "event_id": "a1b2c3d4-0000-11ec-9a03-0242ac130003",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-14T18:22:12Z",
  "event_type": "key.rotate",
  "key_id": "k_7f9e3b2a",
  "key_alias": "payments-prod-aksv1",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "operation_result": "SUCCESS",
  "initiator_principal": "svc-kms-rotation",
  "initiator_role": "kms-operator",
  "auth_method": "mTLS",
  "policy_evaluation_id": "pe-20250214-87",
  "audit_proof_crc": "3adf9c7b",
  "hsm_slot": "hsm-a-02",
  "kms_node": "node-rlw-17",
  "rotation_policy_version": "1.4.0",
  "kms_build_sha": "sha256:9f9e..."
}

SIEM export mapping (ECS-aligned recommendations):
- ecs.timestamp <- timestamp
- event.id <- event_id
- event.action <- event_type
- kubernetes.namespace or service.name <- "redwood-kms-runtime" (set static)
- host.name <- kms_node
- user.id <- initiator_principal
- user.name <- initiator_role
- threat.indicator.hash <- audit_proof_crc (as evidence checksum)
- labels.tenant_id <- tenant_id
- elasticsearch ingest pipeline should tag 'sensitive:true' for key.* events for retention rules

Evidence packaging and notarization pipeline (workflow):
1) Event emitted to internal audit-event-stream and persisted to WAL.
2) Evidence collector aggregates artifacts for the event_id within window T (default 5s):
   - Operation request/response payloads (redacted)
   - Policy evaluation decision object (policy_evaluation_id)
   - KMS node logs covering the transaction (bounded by 10s before/after)
   - HSM audit digest (if HSM involvement) or cloud-KMS API trace (if BYOK shim used)
   - Signed rotation transaction record from rotation coordinator
3) Collector builds an evidence bundle tar.gz with a manifest.txt containing checksums.
4) Bundle is signed with a rotating platform signing key (svc-rotation-signer) using RSASSA-PSS. Signature metadata added to manifest.
5) Bundle is stored in immutable evidence bucket (S3 w/ object-lock) under path: /evidence/YYYY/MM/DD/tenant_id/event_id.tar.gz.sig
6) A webhook event with minimal pointers (event_id, evidence_path, evidence_crc, signature_key_id) is pushed to compliance-subscriber topics.
7) SIEM ingestion picks up the audit event and uses evidence_path to fetch bundles on-demand (RBAC enforced read).

Packaging manifest sample (manifest.txt):
- event_id: a1b2c3d4-0000-11ec-9a03-0242ac130003
- created_at: 2025-02-14T18:22:12Z
- files:
  - request.json : sha256:...
  - response.json : sha256:...
  - policy.json : sha256:...
  - node.log : sha256:...
  - hsm.digest : sha256:...
- bundle_crc: 3adf9c7b
- signer_key_id: rot-signer-v3
- signature_alg: RSASSA-PSS

Automated rotation orchestration (playbook):
- Trigger types: scheduled_policy, manual_request, emergency
- For scheduled_policy:
  1) rotation-coordinator checks rotation policy and selects rotation window (UTC), calculates impact heatmap (active sessions, avg token TTL).
  2) Pre-rotation smoke test: deploy temporary wrapped-key alias and run decrypt/reencrypt on sample quotas.
  3) Orchestrate rollout in waves by tenant risk-class (non-critical -> standard -> critical).
  4) After each wave, run smoke verification and capture evidence bundle; if verification fails, auto-rollback to previous key version and generate incident audit event.
- For manual_request: requires initiator + approver based on RBAC v2 MFA policy (2-person auth).
- For emergency: emergency-rotation requires crypto-escrow token and audit-notify to legal+security; rotation executes immediately and system enters 'degraded-read-only' for affected keys until full verification.

HSM fallback and BYOK special cases:
- HSM offline: operations that require HSM digital signing (e.g., attestation) fail closed for tenant-escrowed keys; for operational rotation we may use a temporary software-backed wrapping key only after legal/ops approval and with intensified evidence capture.
- BYOK import: importer must provide an import token and key-transport envelope. The import process emits two events: key.import.request and key.import.complete. Import completes only after verification of key material checksum and owner binding. Evidence bundle MUST include customer-provided proof-of-origin and a signed import receipt.

Encryption-at-rest design notes (tenant-aware envelope patterns):
- Storage tiers:
  - cold-archive: AES256-GCM with tenant-wrapped key; rotation cadence: 180 days
  - standard-block-storage: AES256-GCM with per-volume data key wrapped by tenant master key or platform master key per tenant; rotation cadence: 90 days
  - ephemeral-cache: AES128-GCM for performance with frequent key churn (24h) and short-lived KDF-derived data keys
- Envelope strategy:
  - DataKey = random(256)
  - CiphertextBlob = Encrypt(Data, DataKey)
  - WrappedKey = KMS.WrapKey(MasterKey, DataKey)
  - Storage record contains: wrapped_key_id, wrapped_key_blob, algorithm, key_version, key_alias, kms_audit_ref
- Versioning and replay resistance: key_version is monotonic; any rewrap operation must increment version and leave old wrapped blobs immutable. Rewraps emit key.rewrap events with prior_version and new_version fields in audit extras.

Compliance reporting and queries:
- Common queries auditors will run:
  - Show all rotations for key_id within date range (returns event_ids, evidence_paths).
  - For each rotation event, show policy_evaluation_id and policy JSON.
  - List manual rotates and approver ids (ensure 2-person approval logs exist).
- Report format: CSV with columns [event_id,event_type,timestamp,key_id,initiator_principal,initiator_role,operation_result,evidence_path,signer_key_id]

Operational runbook snippets (CLI examples):
- Force rotation (operator):
  redwood kms rotate --key k_7f9e3b2a --reason "security-audit-2025-02" --approve-by svc-sre-ops --mfa-token <token>
- Fetch evidence bundle (auditor):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evidence/evidence/2025/02/14/tenant-42/a1b2c3d4-0000-11ec-9a03-0242ac130003.tar.gz.sig ./ --profile compliance-readonly

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing policy_evaluation_id: treat event as non-compliant; raise ticket and quarantine key actions until reconciled.
- Evidence bundle checksum mismatch: trigger integrity incident and lock affected key versions.
- SIEM backpressure: buffer events to durable queue and mark events as 'siem_pending' in audit store; collectors should retry with exponential backoff.

Open decisions / TODOs:
- Signed attestation schema for HSM-produced digests — finalize fields and ASN.1 profile.
- Retention periods for evidence bundles per region and tenant regulatory requirements (currently provisional: 7 years for enterprise-high, 1 year for standard).
- Define exact RBAC v2 policy expression language extension for 'approval-chains' for manual rotates.

Appendix A: Short glossary
- Evidence bundle: signed archive of artifacts for one audit event.
- Rotation coordinator: service that sequences rotations and signing.
- Policy evaluation id: internal id pointing to the policy engine decision blob.
- BYOK: Bring Your Own Key
- HSM fallback: controlled behavior when hardware module is unavailable.

Appendix B: Quick checklist for audit readiness (operator):
- [ ] Confirm rotation policy version is set and matches org policy
- [ ] Validate RBAC owners for keys to be rotated
- [ ] Run pre-rotation smoke tests and collect sample evidence
- [ ] Ensure evidence-bucket lifecycle and object-lock are configured
- [ ] Confirm SIEM ingest pipeline has healthy backlog
- [ ] Schedule post-rotation validation window and notify customers if tenant-impacting

Contact and escalation: security-oncall@redwood.ai, lead: Asha Patel (security-compliance)

Notes: This is a working contract intended to be machine-readable by downstream automation. Comments, suggested field additions, and mappings to existing Confluence artifacts should be added to linked artifact CONFLUENCE-SEC-1284.
